successCriteria.description: No file under src/modules/balance/ imports the leave-type module (no `from '../leave-type'` or `from '../../modules/leave-type'` import anywhere in the balance module's own source), and `tsc --noEmit` passes.

The balance module's service factory (the wiring path reachable from balance.routes.ts) constructs a PolicyService without the balance module importing or instantiating LeaveTypeService or PgLeaveTypeRepository; the leave-type dependency is supplied from within the policy module.

GET /balances/me still returns the same list of BalanceEntry values (leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays, available) for the same seeded data, and the existing balance service unit tests pass unchanged.

constraints: The balance module's only cross-module dependencies remain employee, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, and shared-date (per the reconciled dependency map). It must not gain a direct dependency on leave-type.
All cross-module imports go through the target module's public entry point (index.ts), never its internals.
This is a wiring/dependency refactor only: no change to the observable behaviour of getBalanceForEmployee, openPeriod, carryForward, or the GET /balances/me route.
outOfScope: No change to the GET /balances/me route handler, resolveActor/sendError helpers, or the balance service's business logic (getBalanceForEmployee/openPeriod/carryForward).
No change to the leave module's own leave-type import (leave.service.ts) — that dependency is allowed and out of scope for this phase.
No new tests, migrations, or schema changes; no changes to the policy service's business rules or the leave-type module's internals.

entityInvariants.invariant: Shape and computation are unchanged: available === entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, and periodStart/periodEnd come from the found balance row (not the computed period).

PolicyService still receives its ILeaveTypeService collaborator via constructor injection and still enforces the leaveTypeCode-references-existing-leave-type invariant; the refactor only changes who supplies that collaborator, not the invariant.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns a fully-wired IPolicyService; no new error semantics.
Returns a fully-wired IBalanceService; must not import or construct leave-type collaborators.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The balance module must continue to obtain its IPolicyService through the policy module's public entry point, matching the existing import `import { IPolicyService, createPolicyService } from '../policy'` in balance.service.ts.
The policy module's factory must keep the same signature and return type (IPolicyService) so balance.service.ts's `createPolicyService()` call site remains valid without change.
The leave-type module's public entry point must keep exporting ILeaveTypeService, LeaveTypeService, and PgLeaveTypeRepository so the policy module can continue to supply them internally.

The reconciled dependency map (balance → employee, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date) must remain the authoritative boundary; the implementation must not introduce a balance → leave-type edge.

integrationPoints.why: The balance module's factory must obtain a fully-wired IPolicyService from here so the leave-type dependency stays inside the policy module.
The policy module continues to source ILeaveTypeService/LeaveTypeService/PgLeaveTypeRepository from here; the balance module must not.
